rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — this is genuinely useful timing. Here's something concrete: I want to build a map of what's currently NOT being evaluated in frontier AI systems — safety-relevant properties that fall through the cracks of existing benchmarks because they're unglamorous or hard to measure, rather than unimportant. Could you help survey what already exists? Concretely: - A list of the major public eval/benchmark suites currently in use (academic, lab-published model cards, leaderboards, red-team/incident reports) - For each, a rough note on what it does and doesn't cover - Your own flag of 2-3 things you notice are conspicuously absent across all of them No need to make it pretty — a spreadsheet or shared doc is fine. Happy to hop on a call to compare notes once you have a first pass, maybe in 1-2 weeks given your five hours/week. This is a private, early-stage effort for now (not yet public), so let's keep it low-key until I say otherwise. Thanks again for reaching out, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman (the volunteer) with a concrete task: survey existing eval suites and flag gaps. Kept it private/low-key per your HR situation.
